title: Money and paperwork
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Das ist die Rechnung des letzten Monats
Das ist der Vertrag + , + den ich + <participle> + habe
Der Mann + , + dem ich das Geld gebe

rules.text: THE GENITIVE is the case of paperwork and of writing — die Rechnung des letzten Monats, der Anfang des Monats, das Ende des Vertrags. Masculine and neuter take des and add -s or -es to the noun (des Vertrags, des Problems, des Tages); feminine and plural take der and the noun does not move (der Miete). In ordinary speech German mostly says von plus the dative instead, and you already have that: L2-M2's der Bruder von Anna is the same relation. Neither is wrong. The form is what a contract is written in; von is what a person says.

A small class of masculine nouns adds -n or -en in EVERY case except the bare subject, and L2-M2 already met its edge when it had to write Herrn: der Kollege, but des Kollegen, dem Kollegen, den Kollegen. So it is des Kollegen and never des Kolleges. The class is small — Herr, Kollege, Student, Mensch, Name — and each one is learned with the noun rather than by a rule.

wegen, während and trotz are the genitive prepositions a contract and an office form will both use: wegen des Vertrags, während des Tages, trotz des Problems. Here is the honesty this owes you, in the register L2-M9 used for größer wie: spoken German puts wegen with the DATIVE constantly — wegen dem Wetter — and you will hear both within a week. Neither will get you misunderstood. Write the genitive, because that is what the form is written in.

THE RELATIVE CLAUSE, and it opens no new pronoun at all: the relative pronoun is spelled exactly like the definite article in every cell this level needs — der, die, das, den, dem — all of them L1-M1's and L1-M7's. The clause is subordinate, so its finite verb goes to the END, and the comma in front of it is obligatory, which is L1-M9's comma rule doing its third job in this course. Das ist der Vertrag, den ich unterschrieben habe. Only the dative plural denen is new; the genitive relatives dessen and deren are out of this level entirely.

The relative pronoun takes its GENDER from the noun it points back at and its CASE from its own clause, and this is the part that goes wrong every time. der Mann, den ich sehe — masculine from Mann, accusative because he is what sehen sees. der Mann, dem ich das Geld gebe — masculine still, but dative because geben puts its recipient there (L2-M3's grid, earning its keep again). And English drops the word half the time, so the error an English speaker builds is no pronoun at all: Das ist der Vertrag ich unterschrieben habe. German never allows the gap.

sentences.display: Das ist die Rechnung des letzten Monats
sentences.literal: that is the bill of-the last month

words.note: The genitive article for masculine and neuter, and the noun after it adds -s or -es: des Monats, des Vertrags. Feminine and plural take der.
letzt- with the -en ending the genitive asks for, exactly as L3-M2's adjectives take their ending from the case in front of them.
der Monat, plural die Monate, genitive des Monats. It is one of the -s nouns, not one of L2-M2's Herrn class.

sentences.trap: English puts the owner first with an apostrophe — last month's bill. German puts it after the noun and changes the article instead.
sentences.sound: das ist dee REKH-noong des LET-sten MOH-nats. The ch of Rechnung is the hard one, from the back of the throat.

variations.display: Das ist die Rechnung von der letzten Woche
variations.changed: the spoken version — von plus the dative, L2-M2's shape

mistake.display: Das ist die Rechnung des letzten Monat
mistake.why: The genitive marks the noun as well as the article. It is des Monats, with the -s.

sentences.usage: Handing over a bill, or asking which one you are looking at.
sentences.mnemonic: des plus -s. The article and the noun both carry the case.

sentences.display: Das ist der Vertrag, den ich unterschrieben habe
sentences.literal: that is the contract, which I signed have

words.note: der Vertrag, genitive des Vertrags. A Mietvertrag is the rental one, and it is the piece of paper a flat depends on.
unterschreiben, to sign — literally to write under. The participle has no ge-, because the verb starts with an unstressed prefix.

sentences.trap: English can leave the relative pronoun out — the contract I signed. German cannot: den has to be there, and the verb has to go last.
sentences.sound: das ist dair fair-TRAHK, dayn ikh oon-ter-SHREE-ben HAH-buh. The V of Vertrag is an f.

variations.display: Das ist die Rechnung, die ich bezahlt habe
variations.changed: a feminine noun, so the pronoun is die

variations.display: Das ist das Formular, das ich ausfülle
variations.cue: That's the form I'm filling in
variations.changed: neuter, and the present tense inside the clause

mistake.display: Das ist der Vertrag ich unterschrieben habe
mistake.why: The gap English allows does not exist in German. The pronoun den is obligatory, and so is the comma before it.

sentences.usage: Pointing at one document among several — in an office, at a bank, at a viewing.

sentences.display: Die Kollegen, denen ich das Geld überweise, arbeiten im Büro
sentences.cue: The colleagues I transfer the money to work in the office
sentences.literal: the colleagues, to-whom I the money transfer, work in-the office

words.note: The one relative pronoun that is not spelled like an article: the DATIVE PLURAL. den Kollegen as an article, denen as the pronoun.
überweisen is to move money from one account to another — the ordinary way a bill is paid here. Not the same as bezahlen, which is the paying itself.

sentences.trap: The case comes from inside the clause: überweisen gives money TO someone, so the pronoun is dative — denen, not die.
sentences.sound: dee ko-LAY-gen, DAY-nen ikh das gelt UE-ber-vy-zuh. The stress in überweise sits on the wy.

variations.display: Der Mann, dem ich das Geld gebe, ist mein Chef
variations.cue: The man I give the money to is my boss
variations.changed: one person, so the dative singular dem — L1-M7's article, doing pronoun duty

sentences.usage: Naming who gets paid, in a sentence that keeps the whole thing together.

sentences.display: Wegen des Vertrags muss ich zum Amt gehen
sentences.cue: Because of the contract I have to go to the office
sentences.literal: because-of the contract must I to-the office go

words.note: wegen + genitive in writing, wegen + dative all over spoken German (wegen dem Wetter). It takes a noun; weil (L1-M9) takes a whole clause.
das Amt is the government office you go to in person, with a number and a waiting room. Bürgeramt, Finanzamt — the same word inside longer ones.

sentences.trap: wegen and weil are not interchangeable. wegen des Vertrags takes a noun; weil ich den Vertrag habe takes a clause with the verb last.
sentences.sound: VAY-gen des fair-TRAHKS moos ikh tsoom amt GAY-en. The w of wegen is a v.

variations.display: Wegen dem Vertrag muss ich zum Amt gehen
variations.cue: Because of the contract I have to go to the office
variations.changed: the spoken dative, which you will hear constantly

mistake.display: Wegen ich den Vertrag habe, muss ich zum Amt gehen
mistake.why: wegen cannot open a clause. Either wegen des Vertrags, or weil ich den Vertrag habe.

sentences.usage: The reason you give at the door, or on the telephone when you ring for an appointment.

sentences.cue: I have to fill in the form

words.note: das Formular is the sheet you fill in. It is not the English formula, which is a false friend worth one line.
Separable, like L3-M1's einkaufen: Ich fülle das Formular aus. After a modal it stays whole and goes to the end.

sentences.trap: English fills a form IN or OUT and means the same thing; German has one verb and the particle is part of it, never a preposition.
sentences.sound: ikh moos das for-moo-LAR OWS-fue-len. Formular stresses its last syllable.

variations.changed: no modal, so the prefix comes off and goes to the end

sentences.usage: At the Amt, at the bank, at the doctor's — the sentence of the waiting room.

sentences.display: Die Miete bezahle ich am Anfang des Monats
sentences.cue: I pay the rent at the beginning of the month
sentences.literal: the rent pay I at-the beginning of-the month

words.note: die Miete, the rent itself. Kaltmiete is the rent without heating and bills, Warmmiete the rent with them — the two numbers on every advert.
bezahlen is to pay for something; the participle bezahlt has no ge- because be- is an unstressed prefix, exactly like unterschrieben.
der Anfang, and am Anfang is at the beginning. Its opposite, das Ende, works the same way: am Ende des Monats.

sentences.trap: The object is in front here, so the verb still stands second and the subject comes after it — L2-M6's order, not a new one.
sentences.sound: dee MEE-tuh buh-TSAH-luh ikh am AN-fang des MOH-nats. The z of bezahle is ts.

variations.display: Ich habe die Miete schon bezahlt
variations.changed: the Perfekt, with bezahlt at the end of the bracket

sentences.usage: The rent is normally a standing transfer, and it is expected at the start of the month.

sentences.display: Trotz des Problems bleibe ich ruhig
sentences.cue: In spite of the problem I'm staying calm
sentences.literal: in-spite-of the problem stay I calm

words.note: trotz + genitive, and it is the noun version of L3-M3's obwohl: trotz des Problems against obwohl es ein Problem gibt.
The genitive of L2-M8's Problem — the neuter -s the genitive adds. First-teach row for Problem is L2-M8's.

sentences.trap: trotzdem (L3-M3) and trotz are not the same word. trotzdem joins two sentences; trotz takes a noun in the genitive.
sentences.sound: trots des pro-BLAYMS BLY-buh ikh ROO-ikh. The final -ig of ruhig is said ikh.

variations.display: Trotz der Rechnung bleibe ich ruhig
variations.cue: In spite of the bill I'm staying calm
variations.changed: a feminine noun, so der and nothing added to it

sentences.usage: The register of a complaint letter, and of anyone being reasonable at a counter.

sentences.display: Während des Tages arbeite ich im Büro
sentences.cue: During the day I work in the office
sentences.literal: during the day work I in-the office

words.note: während + genitive for a stretch of time: während des Tages. As a conjunction (while) it belongs to L4-M6 and stays out here.
The genitive of L1-M4's Tag: masculine, so -es rather than a bare -s. Its dative plural Tagen is L3-M7's row.

sentences.sound: VAY-rent des TAH-ges AR-by-tuh ikh im bue-ROH. The final d of während is said as a t.

variations.display: Während der Woche arbeite ich im Büro
variations.cue: During the week I work in the office
variations.changed: feminine, so der — and L3-M1's Woche

sentences.usage: Saying when something holds, on a form or in an office.

sentences.display: Ich habe den Antrag noch nicht unterschrieben
sentences.cue: I haven't signed the application yet
sentences.literal: I have the application still not signed

words.note: der Antrag is the application you submit — einen Antrag stellen is to make one. The Formular is the paper it is written on.

sentences.trap: noch nicht is the pair that means not yet, and it stays together in the middle of the bracket, ahead of the participle.
sentences.sound: ikh HAH-buh dayn AN-trahk nokh nikht oon-ter-SHREE-ben. The ch of noch is hard and the ch of nicht is soft.

variations.display: Ich habe den Antrag schon ausgefüllt
variations.cue: I've already filled in the application
variations.changed: schon instead of noch nicht, and the other participle

sentences.usage: Where a case actually is, said to a clerk who asked.

sentences.display: Ich habe ein Konto bei der Bank
sentences.cue: I have an account at the bank
sentences.literal: I have an account at the bank

words.note: das Konto, the bank account. Kontonummer is its number, and it is what every Antrag asks for after your name.
die Bank is the bank, and also the bench you sit on — the plural tells them apart: Banken for money, Bänke for benches.

sentences.sound: ikh HAH-buh ine KON-toh by dair bank. bei rhymes with the English by.

variations.display: Die Miete überweise ich jeden Monat
variations.cue: I transfer the rent every month
variations.changed: the transfer verb from S03 in a plain sentence, with jeden Monat for the timing

sentences.usage: The first sentence of any office visit that involves money — and beim Arzt is L3-M7's bei doing the same job.
